title: Finding Sine and Tangent from Cosine in Quadrant IV
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Given that \cos x = 1/3 and x \in [-\pi/2, 0], find the exact values of \sin x and \tan x.

steps.title: Compute Sine Squared via the Pythagorean Identity
steps.explanation: Substitute cos x = 1/3 into sin^2 x = 1 - cos^2 x to get 8/9.
steps.why: The unit circle identity sin^2 x + cos^2 x = 1 relates sine and cosine for every angle.

steps.title: Determine the Sign of Sine in Quadrant IV
steps.explanation: Since x lies in Quadrant IV ([-pi/2, 0]), sin x is negative, giving sin x = -sqrt(8)/3.
steps.why: The y-coordinate on the unit circle is negative in the fourth quadrant.

steps.title: Evaluate the Tangent Ratio
steps.explanation: Divide sin x = -sqrt(8)/3 by cos x = 1/3 to find tan x = -sqrt(8) = -2*sqrt(2).
steps.why: The quotient identity tan x = sin x / cos x cancels the common denominator 3.
